interaction.prompt: Your gap is tight — close enough to reach the carrier with your stick — and you have inside position. Tap the lane you should steer them into, away from the middle.

mc.stem: Your gap is tight — within a stick length — and you have inside body position on the carrier. What is the correct read?
opts: Keep your feet moving and steer the carrier down the boards, away from the middle
Back off to widen the gap so you do not get beaten wide
Stand the carrier up at the line with a big hit
Open your hips to the middle and shadow the carrier into the slot

feedback.right: Yes. A tight gap with inside position is your chance to finish the angle. Keep skating, protect the middle, and steer them to the low-danger boards.
feedback.wrong: Backing off, lunging for a hit, or opening to the middle all give up the most dangerous ice. With a tight gap and inside position, keep your feet and steer the carrier to the boards.

tip: A tight gap means you can reach the carrier with your stick. Keep your feet, hold inside position, and steer them to the boards — never give up the middle.
why: A tight gap with inside position lets you dictate the carrier's path. Keeping the feet moving and protecting the middle forces the play to the boards, the lowest-danger ice.
